floor-repair.description: Diagnosis-first repair for cupped hardwood, hollow tile, lifting LVP and squeaky subfloors in Sarasota and Manatee County. 2026 rates from $95 per plank.
floor-repair.h1: Floor Repair for Sarasota and Manatee County Homes
floor-repair.lede: Most floor failures are diagnosable and fixable without tearing out the whole room, as long as the root cause gets identified before anyone touches a patch kit.
floor-repair.capsule: Floor repair in Sarasota and Manatee County covers hardwood plank replacement, hollow or cracked tile pull-and-reset, LVP seam and plank swaps, and subfloor leveling or squeak elimination. Our 2026 diagnostic visit runs $185, credited toward the repair, with plank and tile replacement typically $95 to $225 depending on material. Most single-room repairs finish in one to two visits.
floor-repair.near_me_html: Floor repair near me calls spike right after a named storm, and we prioritize water-related calls first across the service area: Sarasota, Siesta Key and Longboat Key close to downtown, Venice and Englewood to the south, and Port Charlotte and Apollo Beach at the edges of our 40-mile radius. A same-week diagnostic visit is typical outside of an active storm response, when everyone's queue runs longer. Inland communities file fewer storm-related calls but see the same steady mix of hollow tile, cupped hardwood and subfloor squeaks year-round. See our Venice floor repair page for storm-season scheduling specifics in that market.

sections.h2: Water damage, and how fast it has to be addressed
sections.html:
The EPA's guidance on mold prevention sets the clock: dry out water-damaged materials within 24 to 48 hours, and keep indoor relative humidity under 60%, ideally in the 30-50% range. That window is tighter than most homeowners expect, and often shorter than the time it takes to get an insurance adjuster out after a storm.

Standard homeowners policies don't cover flood damage in Florida. FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program caps building coverage at $250,000 and contents at $100,000, and new policies typically carry a 30-day waiting period before coverage starts, which is why flood coverage needs to be in place before storm season, not purchased after a forecast turns serious.

Whether a wet floor is salvageable depends on material and how long it sat wet. Solid hardwood standing in water more than a day or two is usually a loss; engineered hardwood's plywood core fails even faster. Porcelain and ceramic tile can often be dried and reused if the substrate underneath survives, and glue-down LVP is the most forgiving of the group once dried out and the seams checked for lifting.

Our two-year workmanship warranty covers installation defects like loose seams or hollow-set tile. It doesn't cover flooding, storm surge, or a slab moisture event that happens after the floor is already in, which is where homeowners insurance and NFIP coverage come in instead.

A hollow sound under tile means it's lost its bond to the substrate, not just the surface. Combining causes are the norm rather than the exception: a missing movement joint, thin or inconsistent mortar coverage, or dust and sealer left on the substrate before setting. We test with a tap survey across the whole floor, not just the tile someone complained about, because hollow spots tend to cluster around the same original mistake.

Cracked tile is a different diagnosis. An isolated crack in one tile, away from any wall or fixture, is usually just an impact. A crack that follows a straight line across multiple tiles is almost always the slab moving underneath, and replacing the tile without adding a movement joint at that line just sets the same crack up to come back. Regrouting is a smaller, separate repair from a full pull-and-reset: cracked or crumbling grout lines let moisture behind the tile even when the tile itself is sound, and catching that early with a regrout is meaningfully cheaper than waiting for it to undermine the bond and turn into a hollow-tile call later.

sections.h2: Cupped hardwood and when it will flatten on its own
sections.html: A cupped hardwood plank, edges higher than the center, means the underside is holding more moisture than the top, and the fix starts with the moisture source, not the floor. Sanding a cupped floor before that source is corrected removes wood the plank needed once it re-equalized, and the surface crowns instead. Mild cupping often flattens on its own over a few weeks to a few months once humidity is back to normal and the source is fixed; we don't recommend sanding until moisture-meter readings confirm the floor has stabilized. Older wide-plank hardwood installs sometimes develop seasonal gaps wide enough to catch a heel, separate from the cupping issue; we fill those with a color-matched filler rather than replacing planks, since the gaps are a normal seasonal-movement response on a legacy install rather than a sign of ongoing failure.

Most squeaks come from above, not below, and most of ours get fixed without opening the ceiling underneath: screwing the subfloor down through the finished floor at the joist line, or injecting adhesive under a loose spot, handles the majority of calls. A slab with dips or low spots is a different problem. Professional self-leveling compound runs roughly $3 to $9 per square foot in typical use, and a 50-pound bag covers about 50 square feet at 1/8 inch thick or 12 to 15 square feet at 1/2 inch, which is why a low spot the size of a dinner table costs a lot less to fix than an entire room out of level. Threshold and transition-strip repair often gets bundled into a subfloor visit, since a loose transition strip and a squeak nearby frequently share the same root cause: a subfloor fastener that backed out under repeated foot traffic at a doorway.

See our slab leveling page for the full process, including how we test flatness before recommending it. For a room where the leveling is more extensive than a spot repair, that's usually a better fit than treating it as a floor-repair line item.

A lifting LVP seam is almost always a glue-down installation losing adhesion at the edge, usually from moisture working up through a slab that wasn't fully cured or tested before the original install. We re-bond the seam with the appropriate adhesive rather than replacing the whole plank when the plank itself is undamaged, which keeps the repair cost and disruption down.

Individual damaged planks, scratched, gouged, or discolored from sun exposure, get swapped from stocked attic material when a client saved extra boxes from the original install, or from a close color match we source separately when they didn't. Click-lock planks toward the middle of a room take longer to swap than ones near a wall, since neighboring rows sometimes need to come up and go back down to reach them. Matching an exact plank color gets harder the longer a floor has been down and sun-fading has moved it away from the original box sample, which is why we bring a physical plank to match against rather than relying on a product name alone.

sections.h2: What a repair typically costs and how fast we respond
sections.html:
Every repair call starts with a $185 diagnostic visit, credited toward the repair once we scope the work. From there, hardwood plank replacement runs $95 to $225 per plank depending on species and match difficulty, cracked tile replacement $95 to $185 per tile, and regrouting $3.50 to $7 per square foot; our floor repair cost guide breaks down typical ranges by issue type. Most single-issue repairs, one damaged plank, a section of hollow tile, a squeaky stair tread, get scheduled and finished within a week of the diagnostic visit. A typical example: a 1970s block home near Gulf Gate with three cracked tiles from a dropped cast-iron pan and a section of hollow tile discovered during the same visit. The diagnostic call catches both issues at once, and the repair, tile replacement plus a partial pull-and-reset on the hollow section, usually finishes in a single day once material is on hand.

If the repair reveals a bigger underlying issue, a slab moisture problem, structural joist deflection, or storm-related water intrusion, we'll say so upfront rather than patch around it, and point you to the right next step, whether that's our refinishing service for a floor that's a sanding candidate instead of a plank-by-plank fix, or a full tile or vinyl plank replacement once repair no longer makes financial sense.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover flood-damaged floors in Florida?
faqs.a: Not under a standard policy. FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program is the coverage that applies, with building coverage capped at $250,000 and contents at $100,000, and new policies typically carry a 30-day waiting period before coverage starts. That waiting period is why flood coverage needs to be in place well before storm season, not purchased after a forecast turns serious. Read the full answer.

faqs.q: Can cupped hardwood floors be fixed without replacing them?
faqs.a: Often, yes, once the moisture source is corrected. Mild cupping can flatten on its own over a few weeks to a few months as humidity returns to normal. We don't sand a cupped floor immediately, because sanding before the wood re-equalizes removes material it still needs and can cause the surface to crown once it dries out fully. Read the full answer.

faqs.q: How much self-leveling compound does a low spot in a slab need?
faqs.a: It depends on the depth of the dip more than the square footage. A 50-pound bag of self-leveling compound covers roughly 50 square feet at 1/8 inch thick, or 12 to 15 square feet at 1/2 inch. Professional self-leveling work typically runs $250 to $700 per room, which is why we test flatness and price leveling before quoting the finish floor on top of it.

faqs.q: What does the two-year workmanship warranty cover on a repair?
faqs.a: It covers installation defects in the repair itself, like a re-set tile that comes loose or a plank replacement that gaps. It doesn't cover a new water event, a slab moisture problem that develops after the repair, or damage unrelated to the original work, the same exclusions that apply to a full installation.
